title: tv-app has no JVM test task; its gate only compiles 1,677 lines
body:
## Summary
tv-app had no src/test and no test dependencies, so Session threading, the pairing address, the failure copy and the resources were invisible to every gate.

## Description
tv-app/build.gradle.kts declared only androidTest dependencies; the overlay gate for tv-app is `:core:test :tv-app:compileDebugKotlin`, which compiles the shell and tests none of it. JUnit 5 is now wired the way core wires it (testOptions.unitTests.all { useJUnitPlatform() }, junit-jupiter from the catalog, already in the gradle cache - no network), and tv-app/src/test/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/RenderStatsTest.kt pins the /health render percentiles (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/RenderStats.kt:29-38). Registry: test-harness (gate-scope-is-not-report-scope) - the gate must see the target.

## Flow
- add testOptions + testImplementation(libs.junit.jupiter) + junit-platform-launcher to tv-app/build.gradle.kts
- add RenderStatsTest (3 cases)
- run :tv-app:testDebugUnitTest

## Expected impact
Every later tv-app fix in this round was gated red-then-green by this task (13 tests found 5 real defects before their fixes). Could break: nothing at runtime; test classpath only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - tv-app logic gets a JVM gate
Before: 0 JVM tests in tv-app; :tv-app:testDebugUnitTest had nothing to run
After: 15 tests in 7 classes, 0 failures (after this round's fixes); the first run of 13 found 5 defects
Method: gate - the task run on both sides
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tv-app/build.gradle.kts:80-82 (before: androidTestImplementation only)
ls tv-app/src -> main (no test)
after: tv-app/src/test/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/*.kt, TEST-*.xml tests=15 failures=0
impact: Every later tv-app fix in this round was gated red-then-green by this task (13 tests found 5 real defects before their fixes). Could break: nothing at runtime; test classpath only.
method: gate - the task run on both sides

title: Pairing card "Connecting" ends in a replacement character on the TV
body:
## Summary
tv-app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:4 held a Windows-1252 ellipsis byte (0x85) in a file declared UTF-8; aapt2 compiled it to U+FFFD, so the card read "Connecting" plus a replacement glyph.

## Description
link_connecting is the first thing a viewer sees while the transport starts (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PairingCard.kt:62-64). The merged resource tv-app/build/intermediates/merged_res/debug/mergeDebugResources/values_values.arsc.flat carried `Connecting EF BF BD`. The byte is now UTF-8 E2 80 A6 and tv-app/src/test/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/ResourceEncodingTest.kt decodes every values*/ XML strictly. Registry: i18n/encoding-corruption-ratchet (now conformant: the gate sees the target).

## Flow
- launch the app before the server binds -> PairingCard LinkView.Connecting -> stringResource(R.string.link_connecting)
- aapt2 had compiled 0x85 to U+FFFD -> "Connecting�" on screen

## Expected impact
Every viewer at every launch sees a clean "Connecting..." instead of a broken glyph; a later re-save in another code page goes red. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the string renders as written
Before: 1 malformed byte; compiled resource "Connecting" EF BF BD; ResourceEncodingTest red (strings.xml listed)
After: 0 malformed bytes; compiled resource "Connecting" E2 80 A6; test green
Method: gate - strict-decode test red then green, plus the merged .flat bytes read on both sides
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
xxd strings.xml line 4: ...6e 6785 3c2f ("Connecting\x85</")
values_values.arsc.flat before: 436f6e6e656374696e67 efbfbd
after: 436f6e6e656374696e67 e280a6
impact: Every viewer at every launch sees a clean "Connecting..." instead of a broken glyph; a later re-save in another code page goes red. Could break: nothing.
method: gate - strict-decode test red then green, plus the merged .flat bytes read on both sides

title: No LAN address puts 127.0.0.1 in the pairing QR as a valid invite
body:
## Summary
LanTransport fell back to "127.0.0.1" when the TV had no non-loopback IPv4, so the card drew a full invitation pointing a phone at itself; the no-network state rendered identically to a working invite.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/LanTransport.kt (old lanAddress, `?: "127.0.0.1"`) made pairingUrl() never null, though PenTransport.pairingUrl() is documented as null "while it is still being established" (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/PenTransport.kt:62). The choice is now lanIpv4() (LanTransport.kt:162), null without a LAN address; pairingUrl() (LanTransport.kt:75) is null with it, LinkState stays on Connecting, and the existing 1 s poll (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:85-92) puts the real QR up when Wi-Fi arrives.

## Flow
- TV boots with Wi-Fi not yet joined -> NetworkInterface lists only loopback
- before: Ready("http://127.0.0.1:8765/?pin=NNNN") -> Invite card, QR and address a phone cannot reach
- after: pairingUrl() null -> Connecting until an address exists

## Expected impact
A viewer whose TV has no network no longer scans a QR that cannot work. Could break: tools/device.mjs pinFromLogcat reads the PIN from MainActivity's one launch line, which reads pairing=null when the TV has no network at launch.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the invite only ever carries a reachable address
Before: LanAddressTest: 2 of 3 pass; lanIpv4([]) == "127.0.0.1"
After: 3 of 3 pass; no address -> null
Method: gate - LanAddressTest red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
old LanTransport.kt:142-151 `}.getOrNull() ?: "127.0.0.1"`
PenTransport.kt:62 `/** Where the viewer should point their phone, or null while it is still being established. */`
impact: A viewer whose TV has no network no longer scans a QR that cannot work. Could break: tools/device.mjs pinFromLogcat reads the PIN from MainActivity's one launch line, which reads pairing=null when the TV has no network at launch.

title: Pen count loses connects and disconnects made on another thread
body:
## Summary
Session.penDisconnected() decremented and then wrote the clamped value back as a second step, overwriting any connect or disconnect another pen's IO thread made in between.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Session.kt (old line 74) `pens.decrementAndGet().coerceAtLeast(0).also { pens.set(it) }`. Each pen connection runs PenSessionHost.host on the server's IO threads (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PenSessionHost.kt:44, 106), so the steps interleave. /health's `pens` (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Health.kt:21, the only consumer) drifted. Now one `updateAndGet { (it - 1).coerceAtLeast(0) }`.

## Flow
- pen A disconnects: decrementAndGet 2 -> 1
- pen B connects: incrementAndGet 1 -> 2
- pen A set(1): B's connect is lost

## Expected impact
The harness's /health pen count stays true under concurrent connects. Could break: nothing; the zero floor is kept.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the counter is atomic
Before: SessionPenCountTest (2 held, 4 threads x 200,000 connect/disconnect) ended at 0, expected 2
After: ends at 2; zero-floor case passes
Method: gate - stress test red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: AssertionFailedError: expected: <2> but was: <0> (TEST-dev.telestrator.tv.SessionThreadingTest.xml, first run)
impact: The harness's /health pen count stays true under concurrent connects. Could break: nothing; the zero floor is kept.
method: gate - stress test red then green

title: A burst of transport commands reaches the player as its last command
body:
## Summary
Session carried player commands (remote keys, and the phone's undo/redo via asTransport) on a MutableStateFlow, which keeps only the newest value, so commands arriving within one recomposition were silently dropped.

## Description
One rule, two carriers: pen edits applied every message (Session.edit), while transport commands - including undo and redo, which core routes through TransportPlan (core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/Protocol.kt:95-99) - went through `_transport.value = ...` and `LaunchedEffect(command)` (old tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:162, 194). Two undos, or an undo and a seek that a Wi-Fi stall delivered together, reached the player as the last one. Session now queues them on an unbounded Channel exposed as `commands` (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Session.kt:39-40) and TelestratorScreen collects it in one LaunchedEffect(Unit), planning each against the player as the previous one left it.

## Flow
- phone sends undo, undo after a stall -> both decoded on the IO thread back to back
- before: the state flow holds only the second -> one undo applied
- after: both queued, planned and applied in order

## Expected impact
A viewer's double-undo undoes two strokes. Could break: a burst of two seek+ now seeks twice (it used to seek once); owed: a device run pressing DPAD_UP twice quickly over two strokes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every command is applied, in order
Before: SessionCommandTest: accept(Undo), accept(Undo), accept(seek+) -> 1 of 3 observable (TimeoutCancellationException collecting 3)
After: 3 of 3, in order; edits still bypass the queue
Method: gate - SessionCommandTest red then green; MainActivity consumer compile-checked only
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: A viewer's double-undo undoes two strokes. Could break: a burst of two seek+ now seeks twice (it used to seek once); owed: a device run pressing DPAD_UP twice quickly over two strokes.
method: gate - SessionCommandTest red then green; MainActivity consumer compile-checked only

title: Session's three-thread use had no guard; core pins only one writer
body:
## Summary
The app enters one Session from pen IO threads, the main thread's plan edits and publish, and heartbeat reads; nothing tested that shape, and before pen-core's d6b434e7 it threw.

## Description
Writers: Session.accept -> edit on the server IO thread (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PenSessionHost.kt:63) and session.edit(action.message) on main (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:218); readers: publishIfDirty at 30 Hz and heartbeatInput (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Session.kt). pen-core locked PenEngine in d6b434e7 and pinned it with one writer and one reader; tv-app/src/test/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/SessionThreadingTest.kt drives two writers and a reader through Session, so a Session change that bypasses or splits the engine lock goes red. Registry: concurrency-guards.

## Flow
- 3 threads x 40,000 rounds: strokes via accept; edit(Undo/Redo)+publishIfDirty; heartbeatInput+annotationCount
- assert no throwable and doc size == annotationCount

## Expected impact
The renderer and heartbeat stop being one refactor away from torn reads. Could break: nothing; test only.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the shell's threading is pinned
Before: red on 790372cf (before d6b434e7): ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (Index -1, length 10) and NullPointerException (Metric.apart, parameter a)
After: green with d6b434e7
Method: gate - same test on both trees
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: threads raised: [java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index -1 out of bounds for length 10, java.lang.NullPointerException: Parameter specified as non-null is null: method dev.telestrator.core.Metric.apart, parameter a]
impact: The renderer and heartbeat stop being one refactor away from torn reads. Could break: nothing; test only.
method: gate - same test on both trees

title: A pen server that cannot start prints the exception's text on the TV
body:
## Summary
Two of LanTransport's three failure writes passed the exception message straight to the pairing card, which PenTransport documents as "something a viewer can act on".

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/LanTransport.kt (old 86 `e.message ?: e.toString()`, old 126 `cause?.message`) versus the human sentence at old 132; PairingCard prints the value at 22 sp in red (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PairingCard.kt:74-81); contract at tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/PenTransport.kt:67-73. All three now go through failureMessage() (LanTransport.kt:169): a bind failure anywhere in the cause chain reads the port sentence, anything else "The pen server could not start. Restart the app."; the exception stays in logcat.

## Flow
- server start fails with EACCES -> before: "socket failed: EACCES (Permission denied)" on the TV
- after: "The pen server could not start. Restart the app."

## Expected impact
A living-room viewer gets an instruction instead of errno text. Could break: nothing reads the old text (git grep transportError: no consumer outside PairingCard).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - failure copy is actionable
Before: 2 of 3 failure sites raw; FailureMessageTest red on both cases
After: 0 of 3; 2 of 2 green
Method: gate - FailureMessageTest red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
expected: <port 8765 is in use by something else> but was: <engine failed>
expected: <The pen server could not start. Restart the app.> but was: <socket failed: EACCES (Permission denied)>
impact: A living-room viewer gets an instruction instead of errno text. Could break: nothing reads the old text (git grep transportError: no consumer outside PairingCard).

title: Clip keeps playing after Home: the player has no lifecycle or audio focus
body:
## Summary
The ExoPlayer is built in a remember and released only when the composition is disposed (activity destroy); nothing pauses it on stop, and it does not request audio focus.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:168-176 builds the player with playWhenReady = true and REPEAT_MODE_ALL and releases it only in DisposableEffect.onDispose; Home on a Fire TV stops but does not destroy the activity, so a clip with audio keeps playing behind the launcher, looping. No setAudioAttributes(handleAudioFocus) either, so another app taking focus does not pause it. Registry: media-playback / media-resource-lifecycle - "audio that keeps playing after its surface is gone ... reapers for audible resources are bound to the owning scope's teardown"; a stopped activity is the interruption exit nobody tests.

## Flow
- play a clip -> press Home -> activity onStop, composition alive
- player still playing (REPEAT_MODE_ALL) with no surface
- fix: pause on ON_STOP (resume per the viewer's last state on ON_START), audio attributes with focus handling

## Expected impact
A viewer leaving the app no longer hears the clip from the home screen. Could break: a pen session expecting playback to continue in the background (none documented).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - playback stops with its surface
Before: simulation: 0 of 2 interruption exits handled (stop, focus loss); 1 of 3 exits (destroy) reaps the player
After: predicted 3 of 3; falsified if Fire OS destroys the activity on Home (then the before already stops)
Method: simulation - three exits walked in MainActivity.kt; a device is needed to observe audio after Home
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: A viewer leaving the app no longer hears the clip from the home screen. Could break: a pen session expecting playback to continue in the background (none documented).
method: simulation - three exits walked in MainActivity.kt; a device is needed to observe audio after Home
instrument: device run on the Fire TV Stick: start the app, press Home, then `adb shell dumpsys media.audio_flinger` / `dumpsys audio` for an active track from dev.telestrator.tv and logcat of the 30 Hz loop position advancing; same run after the fix (pause in onStop or on Lifecycle.Event.ON_STOP, setAudioAttributes(..., handleAudioFocus = true)). Lane B because no emulator or device is available here.

title: Thumbnailer's retriever is shared across threads and released mid-decode
body:
## Summary
Thumbnailer.dataUrlAt runs on Dispatchers.IO from each paired pen's heartbeat with unsynchronized cache fields, and release() runs on the main thread in onDestroy, possibly while getScaledFrameAtTime is decoding.

## Description
Callers: tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PenSessionHost.kt:130 `withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { thumbnails?.dataUrlAt(at) }`, one per heartbeat (a superseded pen's ticker stops only at its next loop check, PenSessionHost.kt:126). State: tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Thumbnailer.kt:28-29 lastKeyMs/lastResult plain vars; decode at Thumbnailer.kt:43; release at Thumbnailer.kt:65, called from tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:126 (onDestroy). MediaMetadataRetriever is not documented thread-safe, and release during a native decode is a use-after-free risk. Fix: @Synchronized on dataUrlAt and release (and release skips work after release).

## Flow
- two heartbeats ask for different buckets at once -> lastKeyMs/lastResult interleave, a thumbnail for the wrong frame is cached
- activity destroyed during a decode -> release() on main while IO thread is inside getScaledFrameAtTime

## Expected impact
Removes a rare native crash on exit and a wrong-frame thumbnail on the phone. Could break: a second heartbeat waits for the first decode (tens of ms).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one decode at a time, none after release
Before: simulation: 2 unsynchronized entry points (dataUrlAt from N IO coroutines, release from main), 0 locks
After: predicted 0 concurrent entries; falsified if MMR serializes internally (then no crash either side)
Method: simulation - callers enumerated by grep; MediaMetadataRetriever is an Android stub on the JVM
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: Removes a rare native crash on exit and a wrong-frame thumbnail on the phone. Could break: a second heartbeat waits for the first decode (tens of ms).
method: simulation - callers enumerated by grep; MediaMetadataRetriever is an Android stub on the JVM
instrument: device stress on the Stick: pair two phones (LAN), pause so both heartbeats request thumbnails, then finish the activity while a frame decode is running; count native crashes (tombstones) and logcat "frame grab failed" over 20 runs, before and after @Synchronized on Thumbnailer.dataUrlAt and release. MediaMetadataRetriever cannot run in a JVM unit test.

title: LanTransport says a bind failure never leaves start(); a probe says it does
body:
## Summary
The comment at LanTransport.kt:86-88 says Ktor's BindException does not come out of start() and only reaches the handler; on Ktor CIO 2.3.12 (JVM) it does both, so the handler writes the failure card during retries the loop is about to win.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/LanTransport.kt:86-88 (comment) vs LanTransport.kt:114-131 (retry branch that only works if start() throws). Probe this round (scratch JUnit test, not committed): port held by a ServerSocket, embeddedServer(CIO, parentCoroutineContext = handler).start(wait = false) -> start threw JobCancellationException whose cause chain holds java.net.BindException (isBindFailure() true), AND the handler received BindException. So the retry branch is live, and the handler sets `_failure` (LanTransport.kt:91) for a failure the loop retries; MainActivity's poll (MainActivity.kt:85-92) can paint the Failed card until a later attempt clears it. Device behaviour is unverified, and the comment records a crash fix on Fire OS, so the fix must not be landed blind: risk 4.

## Flow
- previous process still holds 8765 -> portIsFree passes in a race or fails later -> engine.start throws and the handler fires
- handler: _failure = port message -> poll shows Failed
- 300 ms later an attempt succeeds -> _failure = null

## Expected impact
Removes a red "port in use" flash during a normal relaunch, and a comment that would mislead the next person touching the crash fix. Could break: if Fire OS behaves as the comment says, ignoring bind failures in the handler would hide a real one - which is what the device run decides.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the comment and the failure path agree with the engine
Before: probe (JVM, Ktor CIO 2.3.12): start() threw with BindException in the chain, handler also fired; 2 writers of _failure for one bind failure
After: predicted 1 writer (the retry loop); untested on device
Method: experiment - a scratch JUnit probe on the desktop JVM; the Android runtime needs a device
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
PROBE chain=[JobCancellationException: LazyStandaloneCoroutine is cancelling, JobCancellationException ..., java.net.BindException: Address already in use: bind] isBind=true
handler=java.net.BindException: Address already in use: bind
LanTransport.kt:86 "Ktor binds inside its own accept coroutine, so a BindException does not come back out of start()"
impact: Removes a red "port in use" flash during a normal relaunch, and a comment that would mislead the next person touching the crash fix. Could break: if Fire OS behaves as the comment says, ignoring bind failures in the handler would hide a real one - which is what the device run decides.
method: experiment - a scratch JUnit probe on the desktop JVM; the Android runtime needs a device
instrument: the same probe on the Stick: hold port 8765 (adb shell toybox nc -l -p 8765 or a second build), launch, and record whether engine.start throws (with BindException in the chain) and whether the CoroutineExceptionHandler also fires; then the fix (handler ignores bind failures, the retry loop owns them; comment corrected) and the same run: the card must not show "port in use" while a later attempt succeeds.

title: Name tags allocate a Paint per tag per frame inside the draw
body:
## Summary
drawNameTag builds a new android.graphics.Paint (plus a measureText) for every visible tag on every frame, and every annotation re-parses its colour string each frame.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Overlay.kt:156-160 `android.graphics.Paint().apply { ... }` inside DrawScope.drawNameTag; the overlay redraws at the frame loop's ~30 Hz (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:179-188) and Overlay.kt:61-62 parseColor runs per annotation per frame (Overlay.kt:77, 98, 120, 138, 154). StrokeCache (Overlay.kt:206) already shows the house rule: geometry is retained, "a frame costs one draw call per bucket and nothing else". The Death Ride work on this Stick measured GC churn as a frame-time cost.

## Flow
- 3 tags visible, playing -> 3 Paint + 3 measureText per frame -> ~90 Paint allocations/s
- fix: one Paint per tag id in a remembered cache keyed like StrokeCache, colours parsed once per style

## Expected impact
Fewer allocations in the 4 ms overlay budget on the Stick. Could break: tag text size on a resize (cache must key on rect height).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - zero allocations per frame for tags
Before: source count: 1 Paint per visible tag per frame; 1 parseColor per annotation per frame
After: predicted 0 per frame; falsified if the alloc tracker shows Paint absent from the top allocators
Method: simulation - counted from source; a JVM test cannot construct Paint and no device is attached
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: Fewer allocations in the 4 ms overlay budget on the Stick. Could break: tag text size on a resize (cache must key on rect height).
method: simulation - counted from source; a JVM test cannot construct Paint and no device is attached
instrument: DDMS allocation tracker on the Stick (works per memory: death-ride P18) over 10 s with 3 name tags on screen, playing: count android.graphics.Paint allocations from Overlay.drawNameTag before and after hoisting the Paint (and the per-annotation parseColor) into a remembered cache; read /health renderP95Ms on both arms.

title: Link poll and frame loop keep running while the app is stopped
body:
## Summary
MainActivity's 1 Hz link poll enumerates network interfaces on the main thread and, like the 30 Hz frame loop, never stops when the activity is stopped.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:85-92 `lifecycleScope.launch { while (true) { ... transport.pairingUrl() ... delay(LINK_POLL_MS) } }` runs on Dispatchers.Main and calls LanTransport.lanAddress() (NetworkInterface.getNetworkInterfaces, tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/LanTransport.kt:148-155) once a second for the life of the activity, including after Home. The 30 Hz loop at MainActivity.kt:179-188 is a LaunchedEffect with delay(33), not frame-clock based, so it also keeps polling the player. Fire TV is a constrained device (TV, not a battery) - the cost is CPU and main-thread time shared with the pen path.

## Flow
- Home -> onStop
- poll keeps enumerating interfaces on Main at 1 Hz; frame loop keeps reading the player at 30 Hz
- fix: repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) for the poll; address read on Dispatchers.IO

## Expected impact
A backgrounded telestrator stops spending main-thread time. Could break: a pen session that relies on the poll while stopped (the server and heartbeat do not depend on it).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - zero background polling
Before: source count: 2 loops with no lifecycle bound; 1 NetworkInterface enumeration per second on Main
After: predicted 0 while stopped; falsified if Fire OS destroys the activity on Home
Method: simulation - loops enumerated in MainActivity.kt; timing needs a device
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: A backgrounded telestrator stops spending main-thread time. Could break: a pen session that relies on the poll while stopped (the server and heartbeat do not depend on it).
method: simulation - loops enumerated in MainActivity.kt; timing needs a device
instrument: device run: press Home, wait 60 s, then `adb shell dumpsys cpuinfo` / `top -n 1 | grep telestrator` and a systrace of the main thread; same after moving both loops under repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED) and the NetworkInterface read off Main.

title: Pairing card and paired dot sit inside the TV overscan margin
body:
## Summary
PairingCard is inset 24 dp and the paired dot 20 dp from the top-right corner; Amazon's 5% safe zone is 48 dp x 27 dp at 1080p (960 x 540 dp).

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PairingCard.kt:104 `.padding(24.dp)` (Card) and PairingCard.kt:57 `.padding(20.dp)` (Chip), aligned TopEnd by tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:242-245 PairingCard(modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.TopEnd)). Fire TV design guidance keeps content 5% in from each edge for overscan; on a TV that overscans, the PIN digits and the QR's right quiet zone are the first to be cut. The repo states the same rule for its other TV surface (docs/DESIGN-ON-AIR.md:47 "5% safe zone"), though On Air itself governs Study Desk, not the telestrator.

## Flow
- TV with 5% overscan -> outer 96 px cropped
- card right edge at 48 px from the edge -> the right 48 px of the card cropped, QR quiet zone lost

## Expected impact
The QR stays scannable and the PIN readable on overscanning TVs. Could break: the card sits further into the picture by 24 dp.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - pairing furniture inside the safe zone
Before: 3 of 3 corner elements (card, dot, status line at 0 dp) outside the 48 x 27 dp margin
After: predicted 0 of 3; falsified if the Stick reports a density where 24 dp >= 5% (it does not at 1080p/xhdpi)
Method: simulation - the stated rule checked against the dp constants; pixels need a screencap
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
PairingCard.kt:57 .padding(20.dp)  (Chip)
PairingCard.kt:104 .padding(24.dp) (Card)
MainActivity.kt:257 status Text .align(Alignment.BottomStart) with no outer padding
impact: The QR stays scannable and the PIN readable on overscanning TVs. Could break: the card sits further into the picture by 24 dp.
method: simulation - the stated rule checked against the dp constants; pixels need a screencap
instrument: adb screencap on the Stick at 1920x1080 with the invite up and with a pen paired: measure the card's right/top edge and the dot's offset in px; the rule is >= 96 px horizontal and >= 54 px vertical (5% per side). Same capture after padding(horizontal = 48.dp, vertical = 27.dp).

title: The overlay's tv-app gate does not run the new tv-app tests
body:
## Summary
This round added 15 tv-app JVM tests, but the overlay gate for tv-app (and the brief) is `:core:test :tv-app:compileDebugKotlin`, which never runs them.

## Description
.claude/scan-sweep/config.md Gates table, row `tv-app/` -> `./gradlew.bat :core:test :tv-app:compileDebugKotlin`. :tv-app:testDebugUnitTest is a separate task; compileDebugKotlin does not compile src/test. Without the row change the tests built this round (tv-app/src/test/kotlin/...) only run when someone names the task. Registry: test-harness / gate-scope-is-not-report-scope.

## Flow
- a later change breaks Session's command queue
- documented gate: exit 0 (tests never compiled)
- with the row change: SessionCommandTest red

## Expected impact

title: The paired state is a 16 dp green dot with no semantics
body:
## Summary
LinkView.Chip renders a bare Box with a green background and no contentDescription, so the paired state is colour-only and silent to a screen reader.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PairingCard.kt:55-61: Box(...).size(16.dp).background(Color(0xFF2ECC71)...).testTag("pairedChip"). Every other state in the same composable has text (link_connecting, link_lost, link_refused, link_locked) or an Image with contentDescription (link_qr, PairingCard.kt:119) - 1 of 6 LinkView states has no accessible name. The colour is the only signal, and it is the only state where no strings.xml entry exists.

## Flow
- phone pairs -> LinkView.Chip -> green dot
- VoiceView: nothing to announce
- fix: add link_paired string and a semantics contentDescription

## Expected impact
A low-vision viewer can tell a pen is connected. Could break: nothing visible.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every link state has an accessible name
Before: 5 of 6 LinkView states named
After: predicted 6 of 6
Method: simulation - counted from PairingCard.kt; the announcement needs VoiceView on a device or an androidTest
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: A low-vision viewer can tell a pen is connected. Could break: nothing visible.
method: simulation - counted from PairingCard.kt; the announcement needs VoiceView on a device or an androidTest
instrument: VoiceView (Fire TV screen reader) on the Stick: pair a phone and record what is announced for the corner, before and after Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.link_paired) } on the chip; a Compose UI test (androidTest, emulator) can assert the node's contentDescription.
